title: The People Building a Way to Slow Down the AI Race
excerpt: As the race to build ever more powerful AI accelerates, a small group of engineers is working on the technology that could make slowing down possible.
content_html:
In the corner of a nondescript office in Sheffield, a city in the north of England, a compact server full of Nvidia chips is whirring away.

It’s a microcosm of the huge data centers springing up all over the globe: town-sized, energy-guzzling computers that are the worldly manifestations of frontier AI models.

Here in Sheffield, on these eight chips, engineers from the consultancy Amodo Design are piloting a monitoring system that they hope, one day, might find its way into every data center, allaying the fears of AI researchers who are concerned that the technology they are building may destroy the world.

In late July, more than 1,300 employees of frontier AI companies signed an open letter warning that their AI is quickly becoming so powerful that humans may soon no longer be able to control it. Slowing the pace of AI development, they warned, may become vital in order to allow more time for safety research, and thus avert catastrophe. But slowing down, they wrote, is essentially impossible, due to intense competition between companies and countries. The AI race is stuck in an arms-race dynamic, these top scientists say, in which one team slowing down would only hand victory to rivals that don’t.

The letter’s main request—one so important to 1,300 of the world’s top AI researchers that they called publicly for it—was for the U.S. government to support an international effort to build tools that would enable all sides to slow down the AI race. 

So far, only a small group of people are working on this effort. There are fewer than 50 engineers in the world working full-time on building so-called “AI verification” tools, Amodo CEO Tom Milton estimates—nine of them at Amodo—plus a few dozen more policy researchers scattered among a handful of companies and research institutes. Meanwhile, trillions of dollars, and the combined might of the world’s biggest tech companies, are now dedicated to making AI systems more powerful as quickly as possible. Efforts to build slowdown tools are funded mostly by academia and philanthropy. (Amodo’s work in this area is funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund and Longview Philanthropy, two grantmakers that have donated heavily toward reducing AI-related risks.) 

“It is surprising that very few people are doing it,” says Milton, a 28-year-old who fell into the field almost by accident several years ago, when Amodo was commissioned to do some work in the area. 

In Sheffield, three workers are huddled around their compute cluster, under an air conditioning unit that is running on full-blast. Their small-scale prototype may be running hot, but it isn’t ready yet. Many technical obstacles remain in its way, plus a bigger political one: it won’t be useful unless the U.S. and China come to the table and agree on an AI slowdown treaty, Milton says.

For now at least, such an agreement looks unlikely. But Amodo’s engineers are keenly aware that political choices are downstream from what is possible. Treaties that curtailed the Cold War arms race were only possible because new technologies, like satellites and seismometers, allowed each side to verify the other’s compliance. Milton expects a similar moment to arrive for AI. When that moment comes, he wants to be ready. 

How AI verification might work

Nobody knows how an AI slowdown treaty might look, but Amodo’s engineers believe it will probably require monitoring data centers, given that these are the places where AI physically lives. 

The current prototype that Amodo is building could make it possible to gain two assurances about a data center that might be helpful in the years to come, Milton says. 

First, that a data center is only being used for inference. That means the running of existing AI models, rather than the training of new, more powerful ones. 

Second, that a data center is running a particular, agreed-upon model—for example, one that has passed certain safety tests, perhaps ones that have been set down in law.

To demonstrate how this might work, an Amodo engineer logs into the whirring server rack, where he spins up two separate systems, each containing an open-source AI model made by OpenAI. 

Think of the first system, he says, as an AI model that a company would normally run in a data center. The second system is the “verifier,” he explains. Its job is to sample snippets of data from this data center and rerun them on its own version of the model, thus confirming that the model is the one the data center operator claims it to be.

When he demonstrates it, the system works—at least on its own terms. The verifier performs some calculations on the outputs of the original AI model, and spits out a high certainty score that this model is GPT-OSS-120B, which is exactly correct.

The limitations

There are several significant problems that point to Amodo’s solution not yet being ready for prime time. 

For now, it only works with unencrypted data, which makes it unfeasible for the most sensitive workloads, which are routinely encrypted. (Milton says the next version of Amodo’s prototype will utilize “zero-knowledge” cryptography, which would significantly reduce the amount of unencrypted data needed.)

A second limitation is that a system like this would require data centers to be retrofitted, including a process ominously named “network tapping,” which involves copying data from working chips onto other verification systems within the same building. Given that these are some of the highest-security buildings on earth, housing trillion-dollar intellectual property and masses of private data, that’s access that no leading AI company is likely to be willing to grant, at least today. 

But it doesn’t have to be as scary as it sounds, Milton says. There are precedents in the history of arms control—including nuclear and chemical weapons—for international bodies to carry out inspections of sensitive facilities. These inspections can guarantee that a facility is compliant with international law, without revealing the secrets of how it works to adversaries. Amodo hopes to build on these principles, aiming to build a system that would only send low-information signals like “passed” or “failed” outside of the data center’s secure walls.

(Amodo says it plans to open-source all of its work on AI verification, so that all sides can interrogate it, understand exactly how it works, and be confident it lacks security vulnerabilities.) 

Another limitation is that the verifier system requires computing power in order to run. That could substantially reduce the total capacity, and thus profitability, of any data center that hosts it. The system witnessed by TIME required computing power equal to between one-third and one-fifth of the AI model it was monitoring. Amodo’s engineers say they expect to find substantial further efficiency gains, in particular because the system could theoretically be set to monitor only random samples of a data center’s computation, rather than every single calculation, in order to achieve its intended result. 

Milton acknowledges that for now at least, Amodo’s tech isn’t perfect. The idea, he says, is for it to improve significantly over time, ultimately reaching a point where it becomes minimally invasive and maximally privacy-preserving. “We tend to be of the mind that verification mechanisms will ladder up, and they won't be perfectly trustable and perfectly secure on day one,” he says. “Over time, we can get to systems that can be verified in much more detail.”

There are many individual AI researchers, Milton says, who are paid more than the single-digit-million dollar budget for his entire project. A full-scale effort, of the kind that AI workers asked for in the open letter, might quickly result in more sophisticated tools. 

“It is insane for us to think that we are even a noteworthy participant in this,” Milton says. “Let alone one of the largest projects.”

Is it politically possible?

While AI verification tech remains nascent, the acceleration of AI capabilities in recent months has led to a surge of interest in the field.

The Institute for Progress, a think-tank, recommended in August that the U.S. government collaborate with frontier AI labs, chipmakers, and hyperscale data center builders, plus other governments, to accelerate the development of AI verification tools. “If the nuclear arms control precedent is any indication, the ability to verify that agreements are being upheld is often necessary for parties to enter into them in the first place,” it wrote. “Better verification technology would unlock a broader space of possible agreements.”

It is a view shared by the authors of AI 2040, a follow-up to the widely-read essay AI 2027. Their so-called “Plan A” for humanity to navigate the arrival of superintelligent AI safely makes heavy use of data center monitoring technologies. 

And Anthropic recently announced it would devote resources to “help build the systems that a credible slowdown or pause would require.” Those systems, it said in a June blog post, “would enable frontier AI developers to verify that others globally have actually stopped or slowed, and that a bad actor could not use the auspices of a coordinated slowdown to jump ahead in secret.”

Milton says Amodo has held some preliminary discussions with governments about its work, although he declines to say which governments, or to share specifics.

For now, at least, it seems clear the U.S. government does not share the enthusiasm.

“We totally reject global governance of AI,” the director of the White House office of science and technology policy, Michael Kratsios, said in February. “We believe AI adoption cannot lead to a brighter future if it is subject to bureaucracies and centralized control.”

It’s true that since that speech in February, the White House has slightly moderated its approach to AI regulation, having been spooked by the cyber-warfare capabilities of recent models into testing some frontier models before their release. But White House officials remain highly skeptical of heavy-handed interventions in the AI industry, especially ones that might be perceived as allowing for ground to be lost to China. “We refuse to stifle [AI] innovation with overly burdensome regulation,” President Trump wrote in the introduction to a June executive order.

China, meanwhile, appears to still be pursuing its strategy of releasing open-weight models in an attempt to catch up to the U.S. frontier. 

In other words: neither great power is exactly clamoring to agree on an AI treaty. Officials from the U.S. and China are planning to meet in September to discuss the growing risks of AI, Reuters reported, though that meeting is more likely to focus on immediate security issues.

Milton is unfazed by what appears, for the moment, to be the political unfeasibility of putting this technology to use. He expects that more powerful AI models will soon arrive, with scarier capabilities. At that point, he expects, both the U.S. and Chinese governments will be “sufficiently scared”—and might come to the table. That possibility, he says, is likely enough “that money should be spent on building the optionality for it.”

sentences.en: When that moment comes, he wants to be ready.
sentences.zh: 当那一刻到来时，他希望做好准备。

blocks.html_en: How AI verification might work

sentences.en: How AI verification might work
sentences.zh: 人工智能验证如何运作

blocks.html_en: Nobody knows how an AI slowdown treaty might look, but Amodo’s engineers believe it will probably require monitoring data centers, given that these are the places where AI physically lives.

sentences.en: Nobody knows how an AI slowdown treaty might look, but Amodo’s engineers believe it will probably require monitoring data centers, given that these are the places where AI physically lives.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道人工智能减速条约会是什么样子，但阿莫多的工程师认为，考虑到这些是人工智能实际居住的地方，它可能需要监控数据中心。

blocks.html_en: The current prototype that Amodo is building could make it possible to gain two assurances about a data center that might be helpful in the years to come, Milton says.

sentences.en: The current prototype that Amodo is building could make it possible to gain two assurances about a data center that might be helpful in the years to come, Milton says.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿说，阿莫多目前正在构建的原型可以让数据中心获得两项保证，这在未来几年可能会有所帮助。

blocks.html_en: First, that a data center is only being used for inference. That means the running of existing AI models, rather than the training of new, more powerful ones.

sentences.en: First, that a data center is only being used for inference.
sentences.zh: 首先，数据中心仅用于推理。

sentences.en: That means the running of existing AI models, rather than the training of new, more powerful ones.
sentences.zh: 这意味着运行现有的人工智能模型，而不是训练新的、更强大的模型。

blocks.html_en: Second, that a data center is running a particular, agreed-upon model—for example, one that has passed certain safety tests, perhaps ones that have been set down in law.

sentences.en: Second, that a data center is running a particular, agreed-upon model—for example, one that has passed certain safety tests, perhaps ones that have been set down in law.
sentences.zh: 其次，数据中心正在运行一种特定的、商定的模型，例如，已经通过某些安全测试的模型，也许是法律规定的模型。

blocks.html_en: To demonstrate how this might work, an Amodo engineer logs into the whirring server rack, where he spins up two separate systems, each containing an open-source AI model made by OpenAI.

sentences.en: To demonstrate how this might work, an Amodo engineer logs into the whirring server rack, where he spins up two separate systems, each containing an open-source AI model made by OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 为了演示其工作原理，Amodo 工程师登录到呼呼作响的服务器机架，在那里他启动了两个独立的系统，每个系统都包含一个由 OpenAI 制作的开源 AI 模型。

blocks.html_en: Think of the first system, he says, as an AI model that a company would normally run in a data center. The second system is the “verifier,” he explains. Its job is to sample snippets of data from this data center and rerun them on its own version of the model, thus confirming that the model is the one the data center operator claims it to be.

sentences.en: Think of the first system, he says, as an AI model that a company would normally run in a data center.
sentences.zh: 他说，将第一个系统视为公司通常在数据中心运行的人工智能模型。

sentences.en: The second system is the “verifier,” he explains.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，第二个系统是“验证者”。

sentences.en: Its job is to sample snippets of data from this data center and rerun them on its own version of the model, thus confirming that the model is the one the data center operator claims it to be.
sentences.zh: 它的工作是从该数据中心采样数据片段，并在其自己的模型版本上重新运行它们，从而确认该模型是数据中心运营商声称的模型。

blocks.html_en: When he demonstrates it, the system works—at least on its own terms. The verifier performs some calculations on the outputs of the original AI model, and spits out a high certainty score that this model is GPT-OSS-120B, which is exactly correct.

sentences.en: When he demonstrates it, the system works—at least on its own terms.
sentences.zh: 当他演示这一点时，系统就可以工作——至少按照它自己的方式工作。

sentences.en: The verifier performs some calculations on the outputs of the original AI model, and spits out a high certainty score that this model is GPT-OSS-120B, which is exactly correct.
sentences.zh: 验证者对原始AI模型的输出进行一些计算，并给出一个高确定性分数，表明该模型是GPT-OSS-120B，这是完全正确的。

blocks.html_en: The limitations

sentences.en: The limitations
sentences.zh: 局限性

blocks.html_en: There are several significant problems that point to Amodo’s solution not yet being ready for prime time.

sentences.en: There are several significant problems that point to Amodo’s solution not yet being ready for prime time.
sentences.zh: 有几个重大问题表明 Amodo 的解决方案尚未准备好迎接黄金时段。

blocks.html_en: For now, it only works with unencrypted data, which makes it unfeasible for the most sensitive workloads, which are routinely encrypted. (Milton says the next version of Amodo’s prototype will utilize “zero-knowledge” cryptography, which would significantly reduce the amount of unencrypted data needed.)

sentences.en: For now, it only works with unencrypted data, which makes it unfeasible for the most sensitive workloads, which are routinely encrypted.
sentences.zh: 目前，它仅适用于未加密的数据，这使得它不适用于通常加密的最敏感的工作负载。

sentences.en: (Milton says the next version of Amodo’s prototype will utilize “zero-knowledge” cryptography, which would significantly reduce the amount of unencrypted data needed.)
sentences.zh: （米尔顿表示，Amodo 原型的下一版本将利用“零知识”加密技术，这将显着减少所需的未加密数据量。）

blocks.html_en: A second limitation is that a system like this would require data centers to be retrofitted, including a process ominously named “network tapping,” which involves copying data from working chips onto other verification systems within the same building. Given that these are some of the highest-security buildings on earth, housing trillion-dollar intellectual property and masses of private data, that’s access that no leading AI company is likely to be willing to grant, at least today.

sentences.en: A second limitation is that a system like this would require data centers to be retrofitted, including a process ominously named “network tapping,” which involves copying data from working chips onto other verification systems within the same building.
sentences.zh: 第二个限制是，像这样的系统需要对数据中心进行改造，包括一个被不祥地命名为“网络窃听”的过程，该过程涉及将数据从工作芯片复制到同一建筑物内的其他验证系统上。

sentences.en: Given that these are some of the highest-security buildings on earth, housing trillion-dollar intellectual property and masses of private data, that’s access that no leading AI company is likely to be willing to grant, at least today.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这些是地球上安全性最高的建筑，拥有价值数万亿美元的知识产权和大量私人数据，至少在今天，没有领先的人工智能公司可能愿意授予这种访问权限。

blocks.html_en: But it doesn’t have to be as scary as it sounds, Milton says. There are precedents in the history of arms control—including nuclear and chemical weapons—for international bodies to carry out inspections of sensitive facilities. These inspections can guarantee that a facility is compliant with international law, without revealing the secrets of how it works to adversaries. Amodo hopes to build on these principles, aiming to build a system that would only send low-information signals like “passed” or “failed” outside of the data center’s secure walls.

sentences.en: But it doesn’t have to be as scary as it sounds, Milton says.
sentences.zh: 但米尔顿说，它并不一定像听起来那么可怕。

sentences.en: There are precedents in the history of arms control—including nuclear and chemical weapons—for international bodies to carry out inspections of sensitive facilities.
sentences.zh: 国际机构对敏感设施进行检查，在包括核武器和化学武器在内的军控史上已有先例。

sentences.en: These inspections can guarantee that a facility is compliant with international law, without revealing the secrets of how it works to adversaries.
sentences.zh: 这些检查可以保证设施符合国际法，而不会向对手泄露其运作方式的秘密。

sentences.en: Amodo hopes to build on these principles, aiming to build a system that would only send low-information signals like “passed” or “failed” outside of the data center’s secure walls.
sentences.zh: Amodo 希望建立在这些原则的基础上，旨在构建一个仅在数据中心安全墙外发送“通过”或“失败”等低信息信号的系统。

blocks.html_en: (Amodo says it plans to open-source all of its work on AI verification, so that all sides can interrogate it, understand exactly how it works, and be confident it lacks security vulnerabilities.)

sentences.en: (Amodo says it plans to open-source all of its work on AI verification, so that all sides can interrogate it, understand exactly how it works, and be confident it lacks security vulnerabilities.)
sentences.zh: （Amodo 表示，计划开源所有人工智能验证工作，以便各方都可以对其进行询问，准确了解其工作原理，并确信它不存在安全漏洞。）

blocks.html_en: Another limitation is that the verifier system requires computing power in order to run. That could substantially reduce the total capacity, and thus profitability, of any data center that hosts it. The system witnessed by TIME required computing power equal to between one-third and one-fifth of the AI model it was monitoring. Amodo’s engineers say they expect to find substantial further efficiency gains, in particular because the system could theoretically be set to monitor only random samples of a data center’s computation, rather than every single calculation, in order to achieve its intended result.

sentences.en: Another limitation is that the verifier system requires computing power in order to run.
sentences.zh: 另一个限制是验证器系统需要计算能力才能运行。

sentences.en: That could substantially reduce the total capacity, and thus profitability, of any data center that hosts it.
sentences.zh: 这可能会大大降低托管该数据中心的总容量，从而降低其盈利能力。

sentences.en: The system witnessed by TIME required computing power equal to between one-third and one-fifth of the AI model it was monitoring.
sentences.zh: 《时代》杂志见证的该系统所需的计算能力相当于其所监控的人工智能模型的三分之一到五分之一。

sentences.en: Amodo’s engineers say they expect to find substantial further efficiency gains, in particular because the system could theoretically be set to monitor only random samples of a data center’s computation, rather than every single calculation, in order to achieve its intended result.
sentences.zh: Amodo 的工程师表示，他们期望进一步大幅提高效率，特别是因为理论上该系统可以设置为仅监控数据中心计算的随机样本，而不是每一个计算，以实现其预期结果。

blocks.html_en: Milton acknowledges that for now at least, Amodo’s tech isn’t perfect. The idea, he says, is for it to improve significantly over time, ultimately reaching a point where it becomes minimally invasive and maximally privacy-preserving. “We tend to be of the mind that verification mechanisms will ladder up, and they won't be perfectly trustable and perfectly secure on day one,” he says. “Over time, we can get to systems that can be verified in much more detail.”

sentences.en: Milton acknowledges that for now at least, Amodo’s tech isn’t perfect.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿承认，至少目前来看，阿莫多的技术并不完美。

sentences.en: The idea, he says, is for it to improve significantly over time, ultimately reaching a point where it becomes minimally invasive and maximally privacy-preserving.
sentences.zh: 他说，这个想法是随着时间的推移，它会得到显着改善，最终达到侵入性最小、隐私保护最大化的程度。

sentences.en: “We tend to be of the mind that verification mechanisms will ladder up, and they won't be perfectly trustable and perfectly secure on day one,” he says.
sentences.zh: “我们倾向于认为，验证机制会逐步升级，但它们不会在第一天就完全可信和完全安全，”他说。

sentences.en: “Over time, we can get to systems that can be verified in much more detail.”
sentences.zh: “随着时间的推移，我们可以开发出可以进行更详细验证的系统。”

blocks.html_en: There are many individual AI researchers, Milton says, who are paid more than the single-digit-million dollar budget for his entire project. A full-scale effort, of the kind that AI workers asked for in the open letter, might quickly result in more sophisticated tools.

sentences.en: There are many individual AI researchers, Milton says, who are paid more than the single-digit-million dollar budget for his entire project.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿说，有很多人工智能研究人员，他们的薪水超过了他整个项目的数百万美元预算。

sentences.en: A full-scale effort, of the kind that AI workers asked for in the open letter, might quickly result in more sophisticated tools.
sentences.zh: 人工智能工作者在公开信中要求的那种全面努力可能很快就会产生更复杂的工具。

blocks.html_en: “It is insane for us to think that we are even a noteworthy participant in this,” Milton says. “Let alone one of the largest projects.”

sentences.en: “It is insane for us to think that we are even a noteworthy participant in this,” Milton says.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿说：“如果我们认为自己是这件事中值得关注的参与者，那就太疯狂了。”

sentences.en: “Let alone one of the largest projects.”
sentences.zh: “更不用说最大的项目之一了。”

blocks.html_en: Is it politically possible?

sentences.en: Is it politically possible?
sentences.zh: 政治上可能吗？

blocks.html_en: While AI verification tech remains nascent, the acceleration of AI capabilities in recent months has led to a surge of interest in the field.

sentences.en: While AI verification tech remains nascent, the acceleration of AI capabilities in recent months has led to a surge of interest in the field.
sentences.zh: 虽然人工智能验证技术仍处于萌芽阶段，但近几个月来人工智能能力的加速发展引发了人们对该领域的兴趣激增。

blocks.html_en: The Institute for Progress, a think-tank, recommended in August that the U.S. government collaborate with frontier AI labs, chipmakers, and hyperscale data center builders, plus other governments, to accelerate the development of AI verification tools. “If the nuclear arms control precedent is any indication, the ability to verify that agreements are being upheld is often necessary for parties to enter into them in the first place,” it wrote. “Better verification technology would unlock a broader space of possible agreements.”

sentences.en: The Institute for Progress, a think-tank, recommended in August that the U.S. government collaborate with frontier AI labs, chipmakers, and hyperscale data center builders, plus other governments, to accelerate the development of AI verification tools.
sentences.zh: 智库进步研究所在 8 月份建议美国政府与前沿人工智能实验室、芯片制造商、超大规模数据中心建设者以及其他政府合作，加速人工智能验证工具的开发。

sentences.en: “If the nuclear arms control precedent is any indication, the ability to verify that agreements are being upheld is often necessary for parties to enter into them in the first place,” it wrote.
sentences.zh: 报告写道：“如果核军控先例有任何迹象的话，那么核查协议是否得到遵守的能力往往是各方首先签署协议所必需的。”

sentences.en: “Better verification technology would unlock a broader space of possible agreements.”
sentences.zh: “更好的验证技术将开启更广阔的可能达成协议的空间。”

blocks.html_en: It is a view shared by the authors of AI 2040, a follow-up to the widely-read essay AI 2027. Their so-called “Plan A” for humanity to navigate the arrival of superintelligent AI safely makes heavy use of data center monitoring technologies.

sentences.en: It is a view shared by the authors of AI 2040, a follow-up to the widely-read essay AI 2027.
sentences.zh: 这是《AI 2040》作者的共同观点，《AI 2040》是广为阅读的文章《AI 2027》的后续文章。

sentences.en: Their so-called “Plan A” for humanity to navigate the arrival of superintelligent AI safely makes heavy use of data center monitoring technologies.
sentences.zh: 他们所谓的“A 计划”让人类安全地驾驭超级人工智能的到来，大量使用了数据中心监控技术。

blocks.html_en: And Anthropic recently announced it would devote resources to “help build the systems that a credible slowdown or pause would require.” Those systems, it said in a June blog post, “would enable frontier AI developers to verify that others globally have actually stopped or slowed, and that a bad actor could not use the auspices of a coordinated slowdown to jump ahead in secret.”

sentences.en: And Anthropic recently announced it would devote resources to “help build the systems that a credible slowdown or pause would require.”
sentences.zh: Anthropic 最近宣布将投入资源“帮助构建可靠的减速或暂停所需的系统”。

sentences.en: Those systems, it said in a June blog post, “would enable frontier AI developers to verify that others globally have actually stopped or slowed, and that a bad actor could not use the auspices of a coordinated slowdown to jump ahead in secret.”
sentences.zh: 它在 6 月份的一篇博客文章中表示，这些系统“将使前沿人工智能开发人员能够验证全球其他系统是否确实已经停止或放缓，并且不良行为者无法利用协调放缓的支持来秘密跳跃。”

blocks.html_en: Milton says Amodo has held some preliminary discussions with governments about its work, although he declines to say which governments, or to share specifics.

sentences.en: Milton says Amodo has held some preliminary discussions with governments about its work, although he declines to say which governments, or to share specifics.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿表示，阿莫多已与各国政府就其工作进行了一些初步讨论，但他拒绝透露是哪些政府，也拒绝透露具体细节。

blocks.html_en: For now, at least, it seems clear the U.S. government does not share the enthusiasm.

sentences.en: For now, at least, it seems clear the U.S. government does not share the enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 至少目前看来，美国政府显然并不具备这种热情。

blocks.html_en: “We totally reject global governance of AI,” the director of the White House office of science and technology policy, Michael Kratsios, said in February. “We believe AI adoption cannot lead to a brighter future if it is subject to bureaucracies and centralized control.”

sentences.en: “We totally reject global governance of AI,” the director of the White House office of science and technology policy, Michael Kratsios, said in February.
sentences.zh: “我们完全拒绝人工智能的全球治理，”白宫科技政策办公室主任迈克尔·克拉西奥斯 (Michael Kratsios) 二月份表示。

sentences.en: “We believe AI adoption cannot lead to a brighter future if it is subject to bureaucracies and centralized control.”
sentences.zh: “我们相信，如果人工智能的采用受到官僚机构和集中控制的影响，就无法带来更光明的未来。”

blocks.html_en: It’s true that since that speech in February, the White House has slightly moderated its approach to AI regulation, having been spooked by the cyber-warfare capabilities of recent models into testing some frontier models before their release. But White House officials remain highly skeptical of heavy-handed interventions in the AI industry, especially ones that might be perceived as allowing for ground to be lost to China. “We refuse to stifle [AI] innovation with overly burdensome regulation,” President Trump wrote in the introduction to a June executive order.

sentences.en: It’s true that since that speech in February, the White House has slightly moderated its approach to AI regulation, having been spooked by the cyber-warfare capabilities of recent models into testing some frontier models before their release.
sentences.zh: 确实，自二月份的那次演讲以来，白宫对人工智能监管的态度略有缓和，因为对最新模型的网络战能力感到震惊，在一些前沿模型发布之前对其进行了测试。

sentences.en: But White House officials remain highly skeptical of heavy-handed interventions in the AI industry, especially ones that might be perceived as allowing for ground to be lost to China.
sentences.zh: 但白宫官员仍然对人工智能行业的严厉干预持高度怀疑态度，尤其是那些可能被认为会让中国失利的干预措施。

sentences.en: “We refuse to stifle [AI] innovation with overly burdensome regulation,” President Trump wrote in the introduction to a June executive order.
sentences.zh: “我们拒绝用过于繁琐的监管来扼杀[人工智能]创新，”特朗普总统在 6 月份的行政命令的介绍中写道。

blocks.html_en: China, meanwhile, appears to still be pursuing its strategy of releasing open-weight models in an attempt to catch up to the U.S. frontier.

sentences.en: China, meanwhile, appears to still be pursuing its strategy of releasing open-weight models in an attempt to catch up to the U.S. frontier.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，中国似乎仍在推行发布开放重量模型的战略，试图赶上美国的前沿。

blocks.html_en: In other words: neither great power is exactly clamoring to agree on an AI treaty. Officials from the U.S. and China are planning to meet in September to discuss the growing risks of AI, Reuters reported, though that meeting is more likely to focus on immediate security issues.

sentences.en: In other words: neither great power is exactly clamoring to agree on an AI treaty.
sentences.zh: 换句话说：两个大国都没有强烈要求就人工智能条约达成一致。

sentences.en: Officials from the U.S. and China are planning to meet in September to discuss the growing risks of AI, Reuters reported, though that meeting is more likely to focus on immediate security issues.
sentences.zh: 据路透社报道，美国和中国官员计划于 9 月举行会议，讨论人工智能日益增长的风险，不过这次会议更有可能关注眼前的安全问题。

blocks.html_en: Milton is unfazed by what appears, for the moment, to be the political unfeasibility of putting this technology to use. He expects that more powerful AI models will soon arrive, with scarier capabilities. At that point, he expects, both the U.S. and Chinese governments will be “sufficiently scared”—and might come to the table. That possibility, he says, is likely enough “that money should be spent on building the optionality for it.”

sentences.en: Milton is unfazed by what appears, for the moment, to be the political unfeasibility of putting this technology to use.
sentences.zh: 目前看来，使用这项技术在政治上不可行，但米尔顿并不担心。

sentences.en: He expects that more powerful AI models will soon arrive, with scarier capabilities.
sentences.zh: 他预计更强大的人工智能模型很快就会到来，具有更可怕的能力。

sentences.en: At that point, he expects, both the U.S. and Chinese governments will be “sufficiently scared”—and might come to the table.
sentences.zh: 他预计，到那时，美国和中国政府都会“非常害怕”，并且可能会坐到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: That possibility, he says, is likely enough “that money should be spent on building the optionality for it.”
sentences.zh: 他说，这种可能性很可能是“应该把钱花在建立它的选择性上”。

content_html_zh:
在英格兰北部城市谢菲尔德一间不起眼的办公室的角落里，一台装满 Nvidia 芯片的紧凑型服务器正在呼呼地运转。

它是全球各地涌现的大型数据中心的缩影：城镇规模的耗能计算机是前沿人工智能模型的世俗表现。

在谢菲尔德，来自咨询公司 Amodo Design 的工程师正在这八块芯片上试验一种监控系统，他们希望有一天能够进入每个数据中心，减轻人工智能研究人员的担忧，他们担心他们正在构建的技术可能会毁灭世界。

7月下旬，前沿人工智能公司的1300多名员工签署了一封公开信，警告他们的人工智能正在迅速变得如此强大，以至于人类可能很快就无法控制它。 他们警告说，为了留出更多时间进行安全研究，从而避免灾难，放慢人工智能的发展速度可能变得至关重要。 但他们写道，由于公司和国家之间的激烈竞争，放慢速度基本上是不可能的。 这些顶尖科学家表示，人工智能竞赛陷入了军备竞赛的动态，其中一支放慢速度的团队只会将胜利拱手让给不放慢速度的对手。

这封信的主要要求——对于 1,300 名世界顶级人工智能研究人员来说非常重要，以至于他们公开呼吁——是美国政府支持国际社会努力开发工具，使各方能够减缓人工智能竞赛。

到目前为止，只有一小部分人正在致力于这项工作。 Amodo 首席执行官汤姆·米尔顿 (Tom Milton) 估计，全球全职开发所谓“人工智能验证”工具的工程师不到 50 人（其中 9 人在 Amodo），另外还有分散在少数公司和研究机构的数十名政策研究人员。 与此同时，数万亿美元以及世界上最大的科技公司的综合力量现在正致力于尽快使人工智能系统变得更加强大。 构建放缓工具的努力主要由学术界和慈善机构资助。 （阿莫多在这一领域的工作由生存与繁荣基金和朗维尤慈善基金会资助，这两个资助者为降低人工智能相关风险提供了大量捐款。）

“令人惊讶的是，很少有人这样做，”米尔顿说，他是一名 28 岁的年轻人，几年前，当阿莫多受委托在该地区开展一些工作时，他几乎是偶然进入了这一领域。

在谢菲尔德，三名工作人员挤在他们的计算集群周围，空调机组正在全速运行。 他们的小型原型可能正在热销，但尚未准备就绪。 米尔顿表示，它仍然存在许多技术障碍，还有一个更大的政治障碍：除非美国和中国坐到谈判桌前就一项人工智能减速条约达成一致，否则它不会有用。

至少目前来看，这样的协议看起来不太可能达成。 但阿莫多的工程师敏锐地意识到，政治选择是可能性的下游。 限制冷战军备竞赛的条约之所以成为可能，是因为卫星和地震仪等新技术使双方能够核实对方的遵守情况。 米尔顿预计人工智能也将迎来类似的时刻。 当那一刻到来时，他希望做好准备。

人工智能验证如何运作

没有人知道人工智能减速条约会是什么样子，但阿莫多的工程师认为，考虑到这些是人工智能实际居住的地方，它可能需要监控数据中心。

米尔顿说，阿莫多目前正在构建的原型可以让数据中心获得两项保证，这在未来几年可能会有所帮助。

首先，数据中心仅用于推理。 这意味着运行现有的人工智能模型，而不是训练新的、更强大的模型。

其次，数据中心正在运行一种特定的、商定的模型，例如，已经通过某些安全测试的模型，也许是法律规定的模型。

为了演示其工作原理，Amodo 工程师登录到呼呼作响的服务器机架，在那里他启动了两个独立的系统，每个系统都包含一个由 OpenAI 制作的开源 AI 模型。

他说，将第一个系统视为公司通常在数据中心运行的人工智能模型。 他解释说，第二个系统是“验证者”。 它的工作是从该数据中心采样数据片段，并在其自己的模型版本上重新运行它们，从而确认该模型是数据中心运营商声称的模型。

当他演示这一点时，系统就可以工作——至少按照它自己的方式工作。 验证者对原始AI模型的输出进行一些计算，并给出一个高确定性分数，表明该模型是GPT-OSS-120B，这是完全正确的。

局限性

有几个重大问题表明 Amodo 的解决方案尚未准备好迎接黄金时段。

目前，它仅适用于未加密的数据，这使得它不适用于通常加密的最敏感的工作负载。 （米尔顿表示，Amodo 原型的下一版本将利用“零知识”加密技术，这将显着减少所需的未加密数据量。）

第二个限制是，像这样的系统需要对数据中心进行改造，包括一个被不祥地命名为“网络窃听”的过程，该过程涉及将数据从工作芯片复制到同一建筑物内的其他验证系统上。 鉴于这些是地球上安全性最高的建筑，拥有价值数万亿美元的知识产权和大量私人数据，至少在今天，没有领先的人工智能公司可能愿意授予这种访问权限。

但米尔顿说，它并不一定像听起来那么可怕。 国际机构对敏感设施进行检查，在包括核武器和化学武器在内的军控史上已有先例。 这些检查可以保证设施符合国际法，而不会向对手泄露其运作方式的秘密。 Amodo 希望建立在这些原则的基础上，旨在构建一个仅在数据中心安全墙外发送“通过”或“失败”等低信息信号的系统。

（Amodo 表示，计划开源所有人工智能验证工作，以便各方都可以对其进行询问，准确了解其工作原理，并确信它不存在安全漏洞。）

另一个限制是验证器系统需要计算能力才能运行。 这可能会大大降低托管该数据中心的总容量，从而降低其盈利能力。 《时代》杂志见证的该系统所需的计算能力相当于其所监控的人工智能模型的三分之一到五分之一。 Amodo 的工程师表示，他们期望进一步大幅提高效率，特别是因为理论上该系统可以设置为仅监控数据中心计算的随机样本，而不是每一个计算，以实现其预期结果。

米尔顿承认，至少目前来看，阿莫多的技术并不完美。 他说，这个想法是随着时间的推移，它会得到显着改善，最终达到侵入性最小、隐私保护最大化的程度。 “我们倾向于认为，验证机制会逐步升级，但它们不会在第一天就完全可信和完全安全，”他说。 “随着时间的推移，我们可以开发出可以进行更详细验证的系统。”

米尔顿说，有很多人工智能研究人员，他们的薪水超过了他整个项目的数百万美元预算。 人工智能工作者在公开信中要求的那种全面努力可能很快就会产生更复杂的工具。

米尔顿说：“如果我们认为自己是这件事中值得关注的参与者，那就太疯狂了。” “更不用说最大的项目之一了。”

政治上可能吗？

虽然人工智能验证技术仍处于萌芽阶段，但近几个月来人工智能能力的加速发展引发了人们对该领域的兴趣激增。

智库进步研究所在 8 月份建议美国政府与前沿人工智能实验室、芯片制造商、超大规模数据中心建设者以及其他政府合作，加速人工智能验证工具的开发。 报告写道：“如果核军控先例有任何迹象的话，那么核查协议是否得到遵守的能力往往是各方首先签署协议所必需的。” “更好的验证技术将开启更广阔的可能达成协议的空间。”

这是《AI 2040》作者的共同观点，《AI 2040》是广为阅读的文章《AI 2027》的后续文章。 他们所谓的“A 计划”让人类安全地驾驭超级人工智能的到来，大量使用了数据中心监控技术。

Anthropic 最近宣布将投入资源“帮助构建可靠的减速或暂停所需的系统”。 它在 6 月份的一篇博客文章中表示，这些系统“将使前沿人工智能开发人员能够验证全球其他系统是否确实已经停止或放缓，并且不良行为者无法利用协调放缓的支持来秘密跳跃。”

米尔顿表示，阿莫多已与各国政府就其工作进行了一些初步讨论，但他拒绝透露是哪些政府，也拒绝透露具体细节。

至少目前看来，美国政府显然并不具备这种热情。

“我们完全拒绝人工智能的全球治理，”白宫科技政策办公室主任迈克尔·克拉西奥斯 (Michael Kratsios) 二月份表示。 “我们相信，如果人工智能的采用受到官僚机构和集中控制的影响，就无法带来更光明的未来。”

确实，自二月份的那次演讲以来，白宫对人工智能监管的态度略有缓和，因为对最新模型的网络战能力感到震惊，在一些前沿模型发布之前对其进行了测试。 但白宫官员仍然对人工智能行业的严厉干预持高度怀疑态度，尤其是那些可能被认为会让中国失利的干预措施。 “我们拒绝用过于繁琐的监管来扼杀[人工智能]创新，”特朗普总统在 6 月份的行政命令的介绍中写道。

与此同时，中国似乎仍在推行发布开放重量模型的战略，试图赶上美国的前沿。

换句话说：两个大国都没有强烈要求就人工智能条约达成一致。 据路透社报道，美国和中国官员计划于 9 月举行会议，讨论人工智能日益增长的风险，不过这次会议更有可能关注眼前的安全问题。

目前看来，使用这项技术在政治上不可行，但米尔顿并不担心。 他预计更强大的人工智能模型很快就会到来，具有更可怕的能力。 他预计，到那时，美国和中国政府都会“非常害怕”，并且可能会坐到谈判桌前。 他说，这种可能性很可能是“应该把钱花在建立它的选择性上”。
